newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty edges up, depos stay at lombard.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty edges up, depos stay at lombard.

text.p: The Polish zloty inched up slightly against the basket of currencies in early Monday trade as the cash-dry money market continued to siphon off zlotys.

Dealers said that banks kept foreign currency positions to a minimum to increase liquidity on the money market, where one-day rates remained glued around the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent for the third consecutive trading day.

"Last week's zloty strengthening trend continued on Monday as (one-day) money market rates are again around the lombard...and I don't expect to see this change today," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
At 0945 GMT the zloty was at 2.76/2.75 percent from the trading band centre, marginally stronger than 2.73/2.68 percent at opening and at Friday's close.
It was at 2.8590/95 to the dollar, up from opening's 2.8595/10 and at 1.8422/26 to the mark, also up from 1.8430/40.
The money market remained short of funds on Monday with one-day rates again hugging the lombard rate, and dealers expected short-term depos to remain at present levels all week.
"It seems that credit outflows and big demand for cash from corporates shortened bank positions in December and rates could stay high all week," said Malgorzata Sikora of ING bank.
One-month deposit bids were as high as 24.8 percent on Monday, which dealers said signalled that the money market's cash shortage may continue past next week.
At 1000 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 24.90/25.1 percent, flat from 24.90/25.15 percent at 0810 GMT, and tomorrow/next rates were at 24.90/25.10, flat at bid and just down at offer from opening.
